takeaway: Gas under the skin with a sick patient and a wound points to Clostridium perfringens, gas gangrene.

question.text: A soldier has a rapidly enlarging 5-day-old shoulder wound, fever, hypotension and surgical emphysema. Which organism is most likely?

lines.text: Our young soldier has a hot, red, enlarging wound on the deltoid, and he is feverish and hypotensive.
Palpating gas under the skin means surgical emphysema: crackle, crackle.
A clinically unwell patient with gas in the tissues points to Clostridium perfringens.
Perfringens, perfumes gas: a little cloud of bubbles.
lines.say: (laugh) Perfringens, perfumes gas: a little cloud of bubbles.

lines.text: Tetani causes tetanus, and botulinum causes botulism with spreading paralysis.
Staphylococcus aureus causes skin infections like cellulitis, so perfringens it is.
